Revised assessment incorporating Beige Book and SLOOS:
- Policy stance: The March 2019 FOMC statement is balanced but dovish-leaning: funds rate held at 2.25–2.50% with “patience,” acknowledging slower activity and muted inflation, with core near 2%.
- Beige Book labor market: Employment increased across districts with persistent worker shortages in IT, manufacturing, trucking, restaurants, and construction; wage gains broadened for both low- and high-skilled workers, with firms also leaning on bonuses, relocation assistance, vacation time, and flexible work arrangements to attract/retain staff. This supports continued labor-market strength.
- Beige Book demand/activity: Household spending softened, in part due to harsh winter weather and higher costs of credit; auto sales and retail were mixed; tourism steady to modest. Real estate showed mixed signals. Manufacturing faced headwinds tied to softer global demand, tariffs, and trade policy uncertainty. Some districts noted effects from the government shutdown early in the period.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS): Banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans, widened loan spreads, and reported weaker demand across business lending, residential real estate, HELOCs, and construction. Expectations point to further tightening in C&I/CRE and softer loan demand over 2019, with banks anticipating deterioration in some consumer and mortgage credit performance. These dynamics imply a more restrictive credit impulse and align with slower capex and household spending.
- Inflation: Overall inflation eased on energy; measures of inflation compensation remained low; survey-based long-run expectations little changed—consistent with muted inflation pressures in the Beige Book.
- Policy implications: The combination of tight labor markets but softer spending, manufacturing headwinds, and tighter credit supply supports the FOMC’s patient, on-hold stance and tilts risks modestly to the downside relative to the baseline statement.

Net effect vs. original assessment: Beige Book evidence of softer demand and manufacturing headwinds, along with SLOOS tightening, nudges the tone slightly more dovish than previously assessed, despite ongoing labor-market strength.
